findings.title: Spawn-context flusher workers are not killed before replacement
findings.body: Workers are always created from `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`, so production workers are `SpawnProcess` instances. `SpawnProcess` is not an instance of the default-context `multiprocessing.Process` class, causing this guard to be false. When a worker is declared hung, the manager starts a replacement for the same Redis shards without killing the original worker; if the original recovers, both workers can flush and produce the same segments concurrently. The same incorrect type check at line 346 also prevents forced shutdown of these spawned workers. Detect process workers independently of the default context (or explicitly exclude only `threading.Thread`) before calling `kill`/`terminate`.

findings.title: A timed-out join leaves remaining flusher workers alive
findings.body: For multiple workers, once the shared join deadline is exhausted this `break` exits the loop before terminating the current or any later worker. `next_step.join(timeout)` may consume the entire timeout before the loop begins, and waiting for the first flusher can consume it for all subsequent workers. A worker blocked in Kafka `future.result()` will not observe the cooperative stopped flag, so those unvisited workers remain running after consumer shutdown/rebalance and can continue operating on revoked shards. Terminate all still-alive process workers after the deadline rather than breaking out before cleanup.

findings.title: The new flusher process count accepts values that break or defeat the limit
findings.body: `--flusher-processes` accepts zero and negative values. A negative value reaches `SpanFlusher`, makes `num_processes` negative, creates no process-map entries, and then raises `KeyError` while assigning the first shard. Zero is treated as false by `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, unexpectedly starting one worker per shard rather than rejecting the invalid limit. Restrict this option to integers of at least one and validate direct constructor callers as well.

findings.title: The new limit test never exercises the multiprocessing implementation
findings.body: Passing `produce_to_pipe=messages.append` selects the `threading.Thread` branch in `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, so this test only checks the in-memory shard map and starts no spawned worker. The production path added by this change initializes Sentry, pickles a shard-specific buffer, creates `SpawnProcess` workers, and must handle their lifecycle; none of that is covered. Add a test that runs the process branch (with Kafka production mocked or an interprocess-safe sink) and verifies shard flushing and shutdown/restart behavior.

findings.title: The added synchronization delay is a no-op
findings.body: The test replaces `time.sleep` with a no-op at line 15, so this purported 0.1-second wait does not give the asynchronous flusher thread any time to observe the drift and emit a segment. `step.join()` then sets the stopped flag, allowing the worker to exit before flushing depending on scheduling. This makes the assertion race-prone; synchronize on an event, queue result, or a bounded polling condition instead of the patched sleep.
